column1: # NFTBan — DECLARED BINARY-WITNESS SUBJECTS  (v1.229.4 PR-D)
# ⛔ HAND-MAINTAINED. READ, NEVER GENERATED FROM WHAT HAPPENS TO BE DOWNLOADED.
#     FOUND_BINARIES must NOT define EXPECTED_BINARIES — that is the tautology the
#     SLSA subject declaration exists to prevent, and the same shape that let
#     nftban-core silently vanish from SHA256SUMS.
# Every subject listed here MUST be present at witness time and MUST be scanned.
# Absence is a FAILURE, never a skip.
# ⛔ MODE CHANGES SEMANTICS (measured in F1, same subject, same tool, same day):
#     source mode   error = REACHABLE from this module's code      -> 5 error / 2 note
#     binary mode   error = vulnerable symbol PRESENT in the binary -> 7 error / 0 note
#   This witness runs BINARY mode over shipped artifacts, so its claim is
#   "present in the shipped binary", NOT "reachable from source". Never quote one as
#   the other.
# nftban-core-linux-amd64 JOINED IN R2 (v1.229.4). Before R2 it could not be a subject:
# the SLSA builder ran in a separate workflow triggered AFTER this one, so the artifact
# did not exist at verification time. R2 made the builder a job of release.yml, so the
# artifact is present before both the witness and checksum finalization. Declaration and
# reality moved together — the row was added in the same change that made it available,
# never one ahead of the other.
# ⛔ THIS FILE IS ALSO THE CHECKSUM COMPLETENESS AUTHORITY (item 4). Gate 3 requires every
#    subject here to be present and covered by SHA256SUMS. One declaration, two consumers —
#    NOT two declarations that can drift apart.
# ⛔ COLUMN 3 = INTEGRITY AUTHORITY. The two binaries do NOT have the same ground truth,
#    and R2 made that difference load-bearing rather than theoretical:
#      build-checksum   built by OUR build-binaries job, so create-release records its
#                       digest in SHA256SUMS.build and Gate 3 cross-checks the downloaded
#                       asset against it.
#      slsa-provenance  built by the SLSA reusable builder in build-nftban-core. It is NOT
#                       produced by build-binaries, and create-release does NOT depend on
#                       build-nftban-core, so its digest is NOT reliably in SHA256SUMS.build.
#                       Its ground truth is the signed provenance verified earlier in
#                       verify-release, not a build-time checksum.
#    ⛔ WHY THIS IS DECLARED AND NOT INFERRED. Gate 3's cross-check reads
#    `if [ -n "$BUILD_HASH" ]` with NO else — a subject absent from SHA256SUMS.build is
#    silently not cross-checked. Before R2 that was invisible because nftban-core was not
#    in the population at all. R2 puts it in, so without this column the release would
#    publish a checksum for an artifact whose cross-validation quietly did nothing:
#        UNCHECKABLE-BY-DESIGN and ACCIDENTALLY-UNCHECKED would look identical.
#    Declaring the authority makes the second one a FAILURE while allowing the first.
